THE BUSINESS GAP

Why do recorded calls still fail to produce sales insight?

Recording answers whether the conversation was retained, but not who will review it, what matters or what happens next. Manual recall and occasional sampling still leave important customer context outside the workflow.

01

Teams cannot replay every call

Managers cannot listen to everything, while random sampling can miss the conversations that need urgent follow-up or coaching.

02

Generic summaries lack sales structure

A general recap may not distinguish budget, decision roles, purchase timing, objections, competitors and commitments.

03

Analysis remains disconnected from action

Even a useful summary creates little value when it does not reach CRM records, tasks or manager reviews.

FROM CONVERSATION TO ACTION

From one sales call to an actionable follow-up

START WITH THE RIGHT TEAM

Which calls are worth analyzing first?

  • High-value calls contain substantial decision context
  • Long sales cycles require continuity across conversations
  • Managers spend too much time sampling calls
  • Recordings exist but structured customer records do not
  • The organization can establish lawful consent and data boundaries
FAQ

AI sales call analysis FAQ

How is it different from call transcription?＋

Transcription captures what was said. TellWin structures customer state, objections, commitments, next actions and patterns around the sales workflow.

Does it automatically score representatives?＋

It can surface evidence against criteria approved by the organization, but uncalibrated model scores should not replace manager judgment or become the sole performance measure.

Can it connect to our CRM?＋

Start by validating fields, accuracy and usage, then define the write-back scope from available system interfaces. Replacing the CRM is not required.

How is customer privacy handled?＋

A pilot should define notice and consent, purpose, access, retention and deletion. The final approach must reflect local law and company policy.
